subject: Procurement path & card exceptions — Medibio (post-call)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda.park@medibio.com>, Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@medibio.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & recommended procurement paths

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and two suggested paths so we can unblock a small pilot.

Key notes from call:
- Use case: inference for clinical note summarization, ingest <5M tokens/month initially.
- Security: SOC2 evidence required for vendor onboarding.
- Procurement: Medibio has AP policies that may require a PO for larger vendors.

Decision points we need from your side:
1) Preferred payment method for an initial pilot ($2–5k): corporate card vs PO?
2) Who owns the vendor intake form and W-9 (name + email)?
3) Marketplace interest: would you consider AWS Marketplace (faster onboarding) for the pilot?

Suggested next steps:
- If card is acceptable for pilot: we can start immediately once we receive a signed order and W-9; no PO required.
- If PO is required: please share procurement contact and expected PO lead time so we can prepare the vendor packet.

Attachments: redwood-sow-template.pdf (SOW stub), pricing-summary.xlsx (pilot pricing tiers).

Proposed ask for this week: can someone on procurement confirm the card threshold and vendor contact by EOD Fri?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

---
From: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@medibio.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Linda Park <linda.park@medibio.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T16:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & recommended procurement paths

Thanks Soojin — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- AP policy: any vendor engagement > $5,000 requires a PO. Individual card transactions are typically capped at $2,500 per vendor.
- Vendor onboarding: requires completed vendor intake form + W-9 + copy of SOC2 or SOC2 letter.
- Procurement lead: Rachel Nguyen (rachel.nguyen@medibio.com) handles vendor packets.

If you can send the vendor packet and W-9, procurement can start the process. That said, we are open to a short, low-dollar pilot on card if Redwood can keep the first month under $2,500 and provide the W-9 up front. Marketplace route (AWS) could be faster but we need to confirm marketplace billing goes through our AP system — sometimes that adds an integration delay.

Also: can you provide your bank remit details for our vendor setup and a link to your SOC2 report?

Tom
Director, Procurement
Medibio Health

---
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@medibio.com>, Linda Park <linda.park@medibio.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & recommended procurement paths

Appreciate the clarity, Tom — responding with concrete options so procurement can pick the cleanest path: 

Option A — Quick pilot (recommended for speed):
- Scope: 30-day pilot, capped at $2,000 (to fit under your card threshold).
- What we need: signed order form + W-9. We will accept card payment and issue an invoice for tracking.
- Timeline: we can be live within 48–72 hours of signed order + W-9.

Option B — PO route (recommended for volume / multi-month):
- We’ll submit a vendor packet (vendor_packet_medibio.pdf) with bank remit, standard T&Cs, and SOC2 letter.
- Typical PO lead time: 2–4 weeks depending on procurement calendar.

Marketplace (AWS) — alternative:
- Pros: fastest vendor onboarding for many customers (billing through AWS).
- Cons: sometimes adds reconciliation steps for AP; if your team prefers direct vendor billing we should avoid it.

I attached: vendor_packet_medibio.pdf (vendor packet stub), redwood-sow-template.pdf, pricing-summary.xlsx. SOC2 link: https://www.redwood.com/soc2-report

If you’re comfortable with Option A, we’ll send a short order form + DocuSign link and provide the W-9 immediately. If you prefer Option B, please loop Rachel and we’ll start the vendor intake paperwork.

Next step from us: I’ll prepare a one-page order form and DocuSign link; Neha will check the marketplace implications and confirm any delays.

Best,
Soojin
Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@medibio.com>, Linda Park <linda.park@medibio.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call recap & recommended procurement paths (internal note)

Internal note — copying into thread for transparency. Two quick items for our playbook that matter here:

1) Marketplace vs direct: Marketplace can be spun up fast but when customers want PO flexibility they often prefer direct vendor billing. If Medibio is PO-first for >$5k we should lead with a card pilot and parallel vendor packet creation.

2) Pricing & credits: recommend we offer a one-time $500 pilot credit to lower friction for a $2k card pilot. If procurement pushes for PO, we convert credits into invoice line-item (no discount required).

Deal: RBW-2027-MEDI-319 — assign Karthik as AE backup for contract redlines. I’ll draft the one-page order and DocuSign bundle tonight.

-Neha
Head of Customer Success (acting)
Redwood Inference

To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & recommended procurement paths

Thanks everyone. We’ll do Option A (card pilot) to move faster — please send the DocuSign link and W-9. We’ll cap the pilot at $2,000 and treat it as a proof of concept; procurement will start vendor onboarding in parallel.

Procurement asks: once we get the W-9 and vendor packet we’ll kick off the PO process for future months; expect a 2–3 week lead time to complete vendor setup.

Tom

Medibio Health
